title: Any support-tier platform admin can read every tenant's plaintext DB superuser URL from /admin/tenants/:id and query all library data unaudited
what: `@Get(':id')` carries no `@AdminRoles(...)` decorator (only `remove` at :157 has `@AdminRoles('owner')`), so AdminRolesGuard short-circuits to `return true` for any authenticated admin. The selected columns include `dbUrl: true` (line 126) and `storageUrl: true` (line 127), and the handler returns the whole row as `{ tenant }`. `tenants.dbUrl` is the full Postgres connection string INCLUDING the plaintext superuser password (see tenant-isolation-02). The controller's own docstring at :131-135 asserts the opposite: "Read endpoints are metadata only - admin must redeem a support key (Step 18a) to see a tenant's actual library data."
impact: The lowest-privileged Libriant staff role (AdminRole.support) — or anyone who phishes/steals one such session — reads and writes EVERY library's members, loans, fines and photos directly in Postgres, with zero support key, zero library consent, zero time box, and zero rows in SupportSession/SupportActionLog. This defeats the entire consented-impersonation control that the support module exists to provide and that the draft DPA/Terms will promise to Greek public libraries. Under GDPR this is an access-control failure over patron PII with no audit trail whatsoever.
evidence:
RAN (probe apps/api/test/integration/zzz-audit-admin-dburl-probe.spec.ts against the live audit env). Created an AdminUser with role='support', logged in at POST /admin/auth/login (Host: admin.localhost) -> 200 {"role":"support"}. Then:
  PROBE2 Q1 status=200 keys=["id","slug","name","defaultLocale","status","primaryEmail","customSubdomain","cellId","dbUrl","storageUrl","createdAt","updatedAt","subscription","billingAccount"]
  PROBE2 Q1 dbUrl returned to support admin = postgresql://libriant:auditpw@127.0.0.1:55440/tenant_cmt5mqcqmcd2cf6fad949cd20f6
  PROBE2 Q1 direct psql with that dbUrl -> members=[{"fullName":"Maria Papadopoulou","email":"maria@example.gr","phone":"+306900000"}]
  PROBE2 Q1 supportSessions for tenant=0, supportActionLog rows=0
  PROBE2 Q2 /admin/tenants status=200 n=23 ; dbUrl exposed for 5/5 sampled tenants
Also READ: admin-roles.guard.ts:36 `if (!required || required.length === 0) return true;`.
fix: (1) Drop `dbUrl` and `storageUrl` from the `@Get(':id')` select, or redact to host+dbname before returning. (2) Add `@AdminRoles('owner')` to the tenant detail read. (3) Longer term, remove the credential from the control row entirely — populate the unused `TenantDbCredential` model with a per-tenant least-privileged role and resolve the password from it at connect time (see tenant-isolation-02).

title: No database-level tenant isolation: every tenant DB is opened with the same Postgres superuser role, and the per-tenant credential model is dead code
what: `urlForDb()` builds every tenant's connection string by taking `PG_SUPERUSER_URL` and swapping only the database name: `const u = new URL(this.env.pgSuperuserUrl); u.pathname = '/'+dbName;`. That string is persisted verbatim to `tenants.dbUrl` and is what TenantPrismaService connects with on every request. The `TenantDbCredential` model (packages/db-control/prisma/schema.prisma:333-346, "Sensitive per-tenant DB role secret ... Postgres role name owning this tenant's DB") is never read or written anywhere in apps/, scripts/ or packages/. Consequently the ONLY thing separating one library's data from another's is application code — there is no role, no GRANT, no RLS, no connection-level boundary.
impact: Every failure that yields one connection string, one SQL injection, one SSRF into the data network, one mis-scoped restore or one leaked backup gives an attacker read/write on all 5-20 libraries at once instead of one. Defence in depth is entirely absent for the asset the product exists to protect. It also makes tenant-isolation-01 and -03 total compromises rather than single-tenant ones.
evidence:
RAN (probe zzz-audit-tenant-isolation-probe.spec.ts P10, live audit env):
  PROBE P10 A role=libriant B role=libriant sameCreds=true
  PROBE P10 connected to B's DB using A's connection credentials: members=0
  PROBE P10 tenant_db_credentials rows: 0
RAN `psql \du` on the control DB: role `libriant` = "Superuser, Create role, Create DB, Replication, Bypass RLS". RAN `select id,slug,"dbUrl" from tenants` — all 17 rows share `postgresql://libriant:auditpw@...`, differing only in dbname. READ: `grep -rn 'tenantDbCredential|dbCredentials' apps scripts packages` returns zero hits outside the schema.
fix: In `provision()`, CREATE ROLE tenant_<id> with a random password, `GRANT ALL ON DATABASE tenant_<id> TO tenant_<id>` and `REVOKE CONNECT ON DATABASE tenant_<id> FROM PUBLIC`, store the encrypted secret in the already-modelled `TenantDbCredential`, and build `dbUrl` from that role. Keep `PG_SUPERUSER_URL` for provisioning/migrations only. If that is too large for Monday, at minimum stop persisting the password in `tenants.dbUrl` (store host/dbname, inject the password from env at connect time) so a control-row read is not a credential read.

title: Every tenant's DB superuser credentials are cached in plaintext in Redis, and production Redis runs with no password
what: `resolveCached()` JSON-serialises the entire `TenantContext` — including `dbUrl` and `storageUrl` — into `lbr:tenant:slug:<slug>` / `lbr:tenant:sub:<sub>` with a 300s TTL, on every cache miss for every tenant. The production Redis is started as `redis-server --appendonly yes --maxmemory-policy allkeys-lru` (infra/compose/docker-compose.prod.yml:372) with `REDIS_URL: redis://redis:6379` (line 37) — no `requirepass`, no TLS, and AOF persistence, so the credentials are also written to the `redis_data` volume on disk. The cache never needs `dbUrl` to be shared across processes; only the id/slug/status/locale lookup does.
impact: A single `KEYS lbr:tenant:slug:*` from anything that can reach the `data` network — the api, worker, migrate, pgbouncer or redis containers, a compromised dependency in any of them, or anyone who reads the `redis_data` volume or an unencrypted host backup — yields the superuser password to every tenant database. No Postgres authentication is involved. The `data` network being `internal: true` is the only control, and it does not survive an RCE in the API process itself.
fix: Stop caching the credential: cache only `{id, slug, name, defaultLocale, status, customSubdomain, tags}` and resolve `dbUrl`/`storageUrl` from a process-local map keyed by tenant id (or from `TenantDbCredential` once it exists). Separately, set `--requirepass` on the prod Redis and put the password in `REDIS_URL`; `redactUrl` in redis.service.ts:62 already anticipates a password being there.

title: TenantGuard authorises on the JWT `tid` claim and never checks the user's actual tenantId, although it already loads the user row
what: The cross-tenant decision is `if (req.session.tid !== req.tenant.id) throw Forbidden` — a comparison between two values that both come from the request (a signed JWT claim and the URL). The guard then reads the user row anyway (`controlDb.user.findUnique({ where: { id: req.session.sub }, select: { status: true, sessionsValidAfter: true } })`) but does NOT select or compare `tenantId`. AuthGuard does make exactly that check (apps/api/src/auth/auth.guard.ts:92-94: `user.tenantId !== session.tid` -> 401), but AuthGuard does not run on tenant data routes — every `/t/:slug/**` controller uses `@UseGuards(TenantGuard, RolesGuard)`. RolesGuard (roles.guard.ts:44-48) likewise looks the user up by id alone and never confirms tenant membership.
impact: The binding between a session and a library rests entirely on a claim minted at login and valid for up to `SESSION_ABSOLUTE_MAX_TTL_SEC` (90 days by default). Any change to `users.tenantId` — a support fix, a future tenant merge/split or 'move this librarian' feature, a bad import, a restore that renumbers rows — silently leaves a live cookie with full read/write on a library the user no longer belongs to, and nothing in the request path would catch it. Today no code path mutates `users.tenantId` (verified), so this is a latent gap rather than an exploitable one; it is filed because the check is free.
evidence: READ tenant.guard.ts:60 (`if (req.session.tid !== req.tenant.id)`) and :79-82 (select omits tenantId), contrasted with auth.guard.ts:89-94 which selects `tenantId` and rejects on mismatch. RAN `grep -rn 'user.update' apps/api/src` — the only writers are staff.service.ts:118/136/148 and login.service.ts:132/191, none of which touch `tenantId`, and staff.service.ts:180-190 `requireManaged` does verify `user.tenantId !== tenantId`.
fix: Add `tenantId: true` to the select already present at tenant.guard.ts:80 and reject when `user.tenantId !== req.tenant.id` with the same 401 AuthGuard uses. Zero extra queries.

title: Suspending a library does not take effect: no endpoint sets the status, and the only way that does (a direct DB update) is served stale from the resolver cache for 5 minutes
what: `suspended`/`archived` is checked in exactly one place — TenantMiddleware — against a `TenantContext` read from Redis with `TENANT_CACHE_TTL_SEC` (default 300s, not overridden in infra/compose/docker-compose.prod.yml). TenantGuard and every downstream service re-check nothing. The resolver's own comment at :53-58 says any code that mutates tenant status MUST call `invalidate()`, but no such code exists: `grep -rn suspend apps/api/src/admin apps/api/src/billing` finds no writer at all. The only admin mutation on a tenant is the irreversible hard delete. So the sole way to pause a library is a manual `UPDATE tenants SET status='suspended'`, which is precisely the path that leaves the cache stale.
impact: An operator suspending a library — for abuse, non-payment, a terminated contract, or a GDPR 'stop processing' demand — sees no effect for up to five minutes across every API and worker process, and gets no error telling them so. During that window the library's staff keep full read/write on patron PII. There is also no supported way to suspend at all short of hard-deleting the tenant and its database.
evidence:
RAN (probe P9a, live audit env): set `status='suspended'` on tenant A directly via controlDb, then immediately issued `GET /t/<A>/members` with A's valid session cookie:
  PROBE P9a after DB suspend, A request -> 200 (403 = honoured, 200 = stale cache)
The response carried the member row created earlier in the probe. READ: tenant.middleware.ts:76-83 is the only status check in the request path; `grep -rn "status: 'suspended'" apps/api/src scripts` returns no tenant writer.
fix: Add `POST /admin/tenants/:id/status` (owner-gated) that updates the row and then calls `tenantResolver.invalidate({ slug, customSubdomain })` — the same pair the hard-delete path already busts at admin-tenants.controller.ts:200-202. Until that ships, add the two `redis DEL lbr:tenant:slug:<slug>` / `lbr:tenant:sub:<sub>` commands to the ops runbook next to the manual UPDATE.

title: The unauthenticated /_files/signed endpoint falls back to SESSION_SECRET for its token signature outside NODE_ENV=production
what: `storageSigningSecret` is `nodeEnv === 'production' ? requiredSecret('STORAGE_SIGNING_SECRET', sessionSecret, nodeEnv) : optional('STORAGE_SIGNING_SECRET', sessionSecret)`. For every NODE_ENV value that is not the literal string `production` — `staging`, `test`, unset/`development`, a typo — the storage-download HMAC key silently becomes the session-JWT key. `GET /_files/signed` runs no middleware-resolved tenant, no session and no role check: `verify(token)` alone decides which tenant's file is served, using `payload.tid` and `payload.ref` (storage-demo.controller.ts:192-203). The code comment at env.ts:340-342 claims this separation exists specifically "so a leaked storage secret can't be turned into a session-forgery oracle and vice-versa" — the guard is keyed on `=== 'production'`, the same pattern the codebase already fixed for cookie Secure (A5-02, env.ts:250-258).
impact: On any deployment whose NODE_ENV is not exactly `production`, one secret grants both session forgery and arbitrary cross-tenant file reads: holding SESSION_SECRET lets you mint a token for any tenant id and any storage ref (member photos and loan/member attachments included) and fetch it anonymously from the internet. Even on a correct production deploy, the two secrets are one operator mistake apart, and there is no boot-time check that they differ.
evidence:
RAN (probe P4d, live audit env). Uploaded a file as tenant A, then with NO cookies at all requested `/_files/signed` with a token forged locally as `jwt.sign({tid: <A id>, ref: 'covers/<file>'}, env.sessionSecret, {algorithm:'HS256'})`:
  PROBE P4d anonymous /_files/signed with token forged from SESSION_SECRET -> 200
  PROBE P4d storageSigningSecret===sessionSecret? true
The 200 carried A's 22 bytes with `content-disposition: attachment; filename="stolen.jpg"`. READ env.ts:343-346. (Mitigating: infra/compose/docker-compose.prod.yml:36 pins NODE_ENV=production and scripts/ensure-env.sh:94 generates STORAGE_SIGNING_SECRET, so the shipped prod path is safe today.)
fix: Require STORAGE_SIGNING_SECRET whenever `nodeEnv !== 'development'` (mirroring `requiredSecret`'s own dev-only carve-out), and add a boot assertion that `storageSigningSecret !== sessionSecret` outside development.

title: Approving a library edit request rewrites tenants.name without busting the resolver cache
what: `approve()` does `tx.tenant.update({ where: { id: req.tenantId }, data })` where `data` is built from the core profile fields, which include `name`. `name` is one of the columns cached inside the `TenantContext` blob (tenant-resolver.service.ts:126-136). Nothing in the approval path calls `tenantResolver.invalidate()`. The same applies to `updateFreeFields` at :66, though none of those columns are cached.
impact: After a platform owner approves a library's rename, every API process keeps serving the old library name for up to `TENANT_CACHE_TTL_SEC` (300s) — in email templates rendered by the notification jobs (`library: ctx.name` in member-notifications.job.ts:224) and anywhere `TenantCtx().name` is surfaced. Cosmetic and self-healing, but it is the same class of omission that tenant-isolation-05 makes dangerous, and the resolver's own TEN-04 comment asks callers to do this.
evidence: READ library-profile.service.ts:181-199 (the `$transaction` block) — no resolver reference is imported into the file at all (`grep -n 'TenantResolver' apps/api/src/library/library-profile.service.ts` -> no match), unlike admin-tenant-tags.controller.ts:75 which does invalidate after touching a cached column.
fix: Inject `TenantResolverService` into `LibraryProfileService` and call `invalidate({ slug: tenant.slug, customSubdomain })` after the approval transaction commits.

title: Host-header (custom subdomain) tenant routing is unreachable dead code: nothing can set customSubdomain
what: `resolveBySubdomain` and `extractSlugFromHost` implement a second, Host-header-driven way to bind a request to a tenant, and TenantGuard/TenantCtx treat a Host-resolved tenant exactly like a path-resolved one. But no controller, service or script ever writes `tenants.customSubdomain` — the only writes in the repo are the probe's own and the admin hard-delete's read of it. The lookup also uses `findFirst` with no `status` filter and no Prisma-level uniqueness; uniqueness exists only as a hand-written partial index (`tenants_custom_subdomain_unique ... WHERE customSubdomain IS NOT NULL`, confirmed in the live DB).
impact: No impact today — the branch cannot be reached because the column is always NULL. It is recorded because it is a live, untested, Host-header-trusting authorization input sitting in the tenant resolution path; the day someone adds a 'set your custom subdomain' feature, this code decides which library a request belongs to based on a header, with a `findFirst` that would silently pick an arbitrary row if the hand-written index were ever lost in a migration squash.
evidence: RAN `grep -rn customSubdomain apps/api/src scripts packages` — every non-spec hit is a read or a select; no writer. RAN `select indexdef from pg_indexes where tablename='tenants'` on the live control DB — the partial unique index is present. RAN probe P2b/P2c: `GET /T/<slugA>/members` with `Host: <slugB>.localhost` returned 404 `Unknown library "pb-fd32a3"`, i.e. the subdomain branch fired and found nothing.
fix: Either delete the subdomain branch until the feature is real, or, when it ships, change `findFirst` to `findUnique`-style resolution, add the uniqueness to the Prisma schema, and reject `customSubdomain` values that collide with any existing `slug` (otherwise `<victim-slug>.libriant.com` can be claimed by another library).

title: Attacks that were executed against the live stack and correctly held
where: apps/api/test/integration/tenant-isolation.probe.ts (audit instrument; kept out of CI, run with --project probe)
what: Recording the negative results so they are not re-tested. Two tenants were signed up against the live audit Postgres/Redis, populated with member PII and a stored file, and attacked from the other tenant's authenticated session.
impact: None — these are the controls that work. The path-based tenant boundary itself is sound: TenantGuard is applied on every one of the 24 `/t/:slug/**` controllers (verified by grep), every tenant data access goes through `TenantPrismaService.getClient(tenant)` with a physically separate database, the LRU is keyed by tenant id with a dbUrl equality re-check, and no controller resolves data from a user-supplied tenant id.
evidence:
RAN, all results verbatim:
  P1  GET /t/A/members with B's cookie -> 403
  P2a GET /T/A/members (case-variant prefix, Express routes case-insensitively but the middleware prefix check does not) -> 400 'No tenant in this request'
  P2b/P2c same with a spoofed `Host: <other>.localhost` -> 404; the path slug always wins over the Host header (confirmed again by P8b: `/t/A/members` with `Host: <B's subdomain>` served A, matching A's cookie)
  P3  GET /t/%74a-.../members (percent-encoded slug; Express decodes the route param, the middleware sees the raw originalUrl) -> 400, not data
  P4b B requesting A's exact storage filename inside B's own tenant -> 404
  P4c GET /t/B/storage/covers/..%2f..%2f<A tenant id>%2fcovers%2f<file> -> 404; LocalDriver.safeResolve (local-driver.ts:111-120) rejects any '..' segment before resolving
  P5a B downloading A's export job via B's URL -> 404; P5b via A's URL -> 403 (tenant-export.controller.ts:63 checks targetTenantId)
  P6  the same Idempotency-Key replayed across both tenants -> no replay; the Redis key is `idem:<tenantId>:<method>:<path>:<key>` (idempotency.interceptor.ts:65)
  R1  (probe zzz-audit-lru-probe.spec.ts) with TENANT_CLIENT_CACHE_SIZE=1, evicting tenant A's Prisma client mid-query by fetching tenant B's -> the in-flight query returned correctly; `$disconnect()` drains rather than aborting.
Also read and found correctly tenant-scoped: import.service.ts:349 (`findFirst where {id, tenantId}`), staff.service.ts:180-190 `requireManaged`, announcement-delivery cache key `announcements:active:<tenantId>:<userId>`, plan cache `plan:effective:<tenantId>`, and the four background jobs (fine-accrual, reservation-expiry, member-notifications, book-metadata-refresh), which build a fresh per-tenant ctx inside the loop and pass it to `getClient`.
fix: No change required. Consider folding P2/P3/P4c/P5/P6 into the existing apps/api/test/integration/cross-tenant-isolation.spec.ts so these stay regression-guarded.
